From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary flag:** The Seller's preamble asserts the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "FINAL". Our playbook records **no written authority from Amelia Frost** for any fallback (cap, claims period or post-completion Riverlark release). Treat the preamble as negotiation framing, not an agreed bargain; the "market context" assertions are the other side's characterisation and do not bind us. Every issue below remains open.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** 20% is a conditional fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the "excess only" mechanic converts the basket into a deductible, materially eroding recovery.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a drafting rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: 24 months.
- Recommendation: **Reject; hold 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the blanket default quietly drags Title/Tax/IP/indemnity claims into the general regime.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Title and capacity go to whether we acquire the shares at all; "administrative simplicity" is no basis to cap recovery of the price at 20%.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject and insert express carve-out.** This is non-waivable under our playbook, and a limitation purporting to cover fraud is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sep 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject DL 1.1–1.2 and Sch 7 general disclosure; require fair, specific disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of each matter.** Whole-data-room disclosure effectively neutralises the warranties.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any seller-knowledge qualifier limited to named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard imputes constructive knowledge of the entire data room and public registers and, combined with general disclosure, would eliminate warranty protection.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence conditions under DD-002 cl 11.3 are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent requiring effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft as a hard CP (effective, unconditional consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions).** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), so "reasonable endeavours" and a consent-on-delivery deeming are inadequate for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release; require payout, direct repayment and releases at Completion.** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded.
- Recommendation: **Require express treatment – line item deducted from price or seller-funded, including on-costs.** Silence in the funds flow means the Buyer inherits the liability post-Completion despite a debt-free/cash-free price.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering non-transfer of IP, title defects and third-party claims, preserving the SOW3 payment cure; request bank evidence of payment or a confirmatory assignment.
- Recommendation: **Broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 fee, keep the cure, and treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.** The real exposure is not the fee but the risk that core Project Materials never vested in the Company.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no breach admitted.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, written updates to Completion, and a specific warranty/indemnity covering the matter without the Buyer being deemed to know it.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; impose preservation, investigation and update covenants and carve DD-006 out of general disclosure.** The facts establish no confirmed breach, harm or notification duty, and no numeric demand should be made in either direction at this stage.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8 does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: assessment of DD-008/DD-011 together for timing, terminability and accrual before Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reserve position and request the renewal terms; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.** The disclosure is too thin to accept the "ordinary course" label or to justify a deduction.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: Title/Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"; limitations apply to "all Claims" unless expressly stated otherwise.
- Buyer wants: distinct regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, none overridden by general-regime limits.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-outs and delete the catch-all default.** The Seller's drafting collapses every category into the 20%/18-month general regime by stealth.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes DD-012 is merely the source relied on and the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract, constitution, board/shareholder authorisations, encumbrance searches (PPSR), share certificates, confirmation of no options/convertibles.
- Recommendation: **Treat DD-012 as insufficient; require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence as a CP.** A seller-supplied internal register proves nothing independently and cannot support a title warranty capped at 20%.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranty positions "settled" under the general regime.
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms kept open for separate negotiation (dedicated warranties/indemnity, separate caps and periods).
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; mark Tax and IP as OPEN.** No agreement exists; the Buyer should neither accept the general regime nor assume unlimited liability pending negotiation.

---

**Overall:** The draft is not a "fair and balanced package" – it reduces the cap, multiplies the thresholds, shortens time limits, abolishes the fundamental regime, caps fraud, and combines general disclosure with constructive knowledge to hollow out the warranties, while leaving Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and title unresolved. Recommend a full mark-up on playbook terms with a cover note rejecting the "FINAL/principal-agreed" framing, and escalation to Amelia Frost only if the team wishes to consider any fallback.
